items.correctedAnswer: CloudTrail records the caller identity, time, API operation, and selected request metadata such as modelId. It does not record the full prompt or every invocation parameter. Use opt-in Bedrock invocation logging when prompt and response bodies are required.
items.reason: The current wording asks which parameters without stating that CloudTrail omits prompt bodies and may omit other values.

items.correctedAnswer: Use approved decision factors, source evidence, and a validated explanation process. Do not treat a model reasoning trace as a faithful or auditable explanation.
items.reason: The keyed recommendation relies on inspectable reasoning traces, which the official sources do not establish as a reliable explanation method.

items.correctedAnswer: Use detect mode for non-blocking guardrail results. Configure a CloudWatch alarm and notification action to notify staff.
items.reason: CloudWatch metrics do not send notifications without an alarm and action.

items.correctedAnswer: Enable invocation logging for the required prompt and response fields. Add application-level user and retrieval identifiers. Set S3 retention controls, encryption, access policy, and size handling.
items.reason: Invocation logging has configuration and payload limits. CloudTrail does not contain prompt bodies, and application identifiers may be needed for the requested audit record.

items.correctedAnswer: Use application instrumentation to attach a team or feature identifier to each request. Aggregate logged token counts by that identifier and reconcile with billing data.
items.reason: Bedrock CloudWatch token metrics do not automatically include application team or feature tags.

items.correctedAnswer: No existing option set provides a built-in near-real-time hallucination detector. For RAG, call contextual grounding checks in the production path and configure metrics and alarms. Use offline evaluation jobs for sampled quality review.
items.reason: The keyed offline evaluation choice does not meet the near-real-time requirement. The current choices do not include a complete production check and alert path.

items.correctedAnswer: Enable Bedrock Agent trace to inspect orchestration and tool steps. Propagate a request correlation ID. Add X-Ray instrumentation to application and tool calls only if distributed service traces are also required.
items.reason: Bedrock Agent trace and AWS X-Ray are different mechanisms. The current key incorrectly assigns agent internals to X-Ray.

items.correctedAnswer: For a fixed-cost-free burst tier, use on-demand inference. Use Provisioned Throughput only for the steady tier if measured utilization supports its hourly commitment. Verify batch pricing for supported models.
items.reason: The stem requires no fixed hourly cost during idle periods, which conflicts with the keyed Provisioned Throughput choice.

items.correctedAnswer: Check the selected model and API for cache support, minimum eligible prefix, cache boundary, TTL, and read/write prices. A 12,000-token prefix may exceed a documented minimum, but a hit and five-minute TTL are not universal.

items.correctedAnswer: Treat AccessDeniedException as an authorization failure first. Check IAM permissions, model access, Region support, and Marketplace prerequisites for the selected model.

items.reason: AWS documentation supports entity masking but does not promise partial redaction that preserves selected digits.
